idiom_name: header dict/list on the message plus a decorator that appends a hop (confluent-kafka headers)
implementation_notes: The trail is ordinary data: confluent-kafka's Producer.produce(..., headers=[('history', json.dumps(hops))]) and the consumer's msg.headers() expose key/value byte pairs, so a decorator around the handler decodes the 'history' entry, appends {name, ts} and re-encodes it - the classic history container and its per-component hooks are replaced by one helper plus a JSON value. Celery-style job queues carry the same list in the task's headers argument. Note that Message.headers() returns None when a message has no headers (and in some producer-callback paths), so treat 'no history' as an empty list rather than an error.
pitfalls: msg.headers() can be None (messages produced without headers, and the produce callback path), so 'no history' must degrade to an empty list instead of a TypeError.
Header values are bytes: forgetting to decode() yields b'[...]' strings that corrupt the JSON on the next hop, and an encode/decode mismatch is invisible until a reader parses it.
An unbounded list grows the message until the broker's message.max.bytes rejects it - trim to the last N hops and keep entries short.
